points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 1707年4月15日，欧拉出生于瑞士巴塞尔。他的父亲保罗·欧拉是一位新教牧师，希望儿子追随自己的宗教道路。然而，年轻的欧拉在数学方面展现出非凡天赋。在巴塞尔大学，他师从著名数学家约翰·伯努利，后者很快发现了欧拉的才华并私下指导他。这段时期奠定了欧拉坚实的数学基础，特别是对微积分的理解，为他后来的研究奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born on April 15, 1707, in Basel, Switzerland, Euler was the son of Paul Euler, a Protestant pastor. His father wanted him to follow a religious path, but young Euler showed extraordinary talent in mathematics. At the University of Basel, he studied under the famous mathematician Johann Bernoulli, who quickly recognized Euler's abilities and provided him with private tutoring. This period laid Euler's solid mathematical foundation, particularly in understanding calculus, which set the stage for his later research.

points.title: 俄国科学院时期
points.description: 1727年，欧拉接受邀请前往俄国圣彼得堡科学院工作。在这里，他迅速崭露头角，两年内就被晋升为物理学教授。1733年，他接替丹尼尔·伯努利成为数学教授。在圣彼得堡期间，欧拉完成了大量重要研究，包括解决著名的巴塞尔问题（求所有自然数的平方的倒数之和），发表关于变分法的开创性论文，并开始深入研究数论和图论。1735年，他因过度工作导致右眼视力严重下降，这一时期的工作强度为他的健康埋下了隐患。
points.descriptionEn: In 1727, Euler accepted an invitation to work at the St. Petersburg Academy of Sciences in Russia. There, he quickly rose to prominence, being promoted to professor of physics within two years. In 1733, he succeeded Daniel Bernoulli as professor of mathematics. During his time in St. Petersburg, Euler completed extensive important research, including solving the famous Basel problem (finding the sum of the reciprocals of the squares of all natural numbers), publishing pioneering work on calculus of variations, and beginning his deep studies in number theory and graph theory. In 1735, he severely damaged the sight in his right eye due to overwork, a period of intense work that would later affect his health.

points.title: 普鲁士科学院时期
points.description: 1741年，欧拉接受普鲁士国王腓特烈大帝的邀请，前往柏林科学院工作。在柏林的25年间，欧拉与腓特烈大帝的关系复杂，国王欣赏他的才华但有时也批评他的实用主义倾向。尽管如此，欧拉在此期间完成了大量重要工作，包括发表超过250篇论文和几部重要著作。他发展了复变函数理论，引入了欧拉公式e^(iπ) + 1 = 0，并扩展了力学和流体动力学理论。他还为普鲁士政府解决了许多实际问题，包括运河设计和货币改革。1766年，随着腓特烈大帝对欧拉的不满增加，欧拉决定返回俄国。
points.descriptionEn: In 1741, Euler accepted an invitation from King Frederick the Great of Prussia to work at the Berlin Academy of Sciences. During his 25 years in Berlin, Euler's relationship with Frederick was complex—the king admired his talent but sometimes criticized his practical tendencies. Despite this, Euler completed extensive work during this period, publishing over 250 papers and several important books. He developed the theory of complex functions, introduced Euler's formula e^(iπ) + 1 = 0, and expanded theories in mechanics and fluid dynamics. He also solved many practical problems for the Prussian government, including canal design and currency reform. In 1766, as Frederick's dissatisfaction with Euler grew, Euler decided to return to Russia.

points.title: 重返俄国
points.description: 1766年，欧拉回到圣彼得堡，被任命为科学院数学部主任。此时他的视力已经严重恶化，几乎完全失明。然而，这并未阻止他的研究工作。在助手们的帮助下，欧拉继续进行数学研究，甚至比失明前更加多产。他发展了月球运动理论，改进了望远镜和显微镜的设计，并继续在数论、分析和力学领域做出贡献。1783年9月18日，欧拉在圣彼得堡去世，享年76岁。在他生命的最后一天，他还在计算气球上升的轨道问题，体现了他对数学的终身热爱。
points.descriptionEn: In 1766, Euler returned to St. Petersburg, appointed as head of the mathematics department at the Academy of Sciences. By this time, his vision had severely deteriorated, and he was almost completely blind. However, this did not stop his research work. With the help of assistants, Euler continued his mathematical research, becoming even more productive than before his blindness. He developed theories of lunar motion, improved designs for telescopes and microscopes, and continued to make contributions in number theory, analysis, and mechanics. On September 18, 1783, Euler died in St. Petersburg at the age of 76. On the last day of his life, he was calculating the trajectory of a rising balloon, demonstrating his lifelong love for mathematics.

points.title: 七桥问题
points.description: 1736年，欧拉解决了著名的哥尼斯堡七桥问题，这被认为是图论的开端。问题涉及普鲁士城市哥尼斯堡的七座桥梁，要求找出一条路线，走过每座桥恰好一次。欧拉通过抽象化方法，将陆地表示为点，桥梁表示为线，证明了这样的路径不存在。这一开创性工作不仅解决了具体问题，还建立了图论的基础，对后来的网络理论和拓扑学产生了深远影响。欧拉的方法展示了数学如何将实际问题转化为抽象模型，体现了数学的普适性和力量。
points.descriptionEn: In 1736, Euler solved the famous Seven Bridges of Königsberg problem, considered the beginning of graph theory. The problem involved seven bridges in the Prussian city of Königsberg, requiring finding a route that crossed each bridge exactly once. Euler used an abstract approach, representing landmasses as points and bridges as lines, proving that such a path was impossible. This pioneering work not only solved the specific problem but also established the foundations of graph theory, profoundly influencing later network theory and topology. Euler's method demonstrated how mathematics could transform practical problems into abstract models, showcasing the universality and power of mathematics.

supporter.zh: 欧拉被公认为历史上最伟大的数学家之一，他的贡献遍及数学的各个领域。支持者赞誉他无与伦比的生产力，一生发表了800多篇论文和书籍，即使在失明后仍保持惊人的研究能力。欧拉公式e^(iπ) + 1 = 0被数学家称为'最美的数学公式'，完美连接了数学中最重要的五个常数。他的工作不仅推动了纯数学发展，还解决了大量实际问题，体现了数学的实用价值。欧拉的严谨思维和创造性方法为后世数学家树立了典范。
supporter.en: Euler is widely regarded as one of the greatest mathematicians in history, with contributions spanning virtually every area of mathematics. Supporters praise his unparalleled productivity, publishing over 800 papers and books during his lifetime and maintaining remarkable research capabilities even after becoming blind. Euler's formula e^(iπ) + 1 = 0, described by mathematicians as 'the most beautiful formula in mathematics,' perfectly connects five of the most important constants in mathematics. His work not only advanced pure mathematics but also solved numerous practical problems, demonstrating the practical value of mathematics. Euler's rigorous thinking and creative methods set an example for future mathematicians.

critic.zh: 批评者指出欧拉的工作有时缺乏严格的证明，特别是在早期著作中。他经常依赖直觉和计算而非严格的逻辑推导，这在当时数学严格化进程中显得不够严谨。此外，欧拉在柏林期间与腓特烈大帝的关系紧张，被批评过于实用主义，有时为了迎合国王而调整研究方向。他的庞大著作中也存在一些错误，后来被其他数学家纠正。批评者认为，欧拉虽然多产，但有时牺牲了深度和严谨性，这在现代数学标准下显得不足。
critic.en: Critics point out that Euler's work sometimes lacked rigorous proofs, particularly in his early writings. He frequently relied on intuition and computation rather than strict logical deductions, which appeared insufficiently rigorous during the period of mathematical formalization. Additionally, Euler's relationship with Frederick the Great in Berlin was tense, and he was criticized for being too pragmatic, sometimes adjusting his research direction to please the king. His extensive works also contained errors that were later corrected by other mathematicians. Critics argue that while Euler was prolific, he sometimes sacrificed depth and rigor, which would be considered inadequate by modern mathematical standards.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，欧拉被定义为18世纪数学的中心人物，连接了牛顿和莱布尼茨的微积分与后来的发展。他的符号系统（如f(x)、e、i、π等）成为现代数学的标准语言。流行文化中，欧拉常被描绘为勤奋工作的天才形象，特别是他在失明后仍坚持研究的毅力被广泛传颂。数学界以'欧拉数'、'欧拉定理'、'欧拉方程'等众多概念命名来纪念他，表明他的影响无处不在。欧拉的工作体现了数学的统一性，将不同领域连接起来，这种跨学科思维对现代科学仍有重要启示。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Euler is defined as the central figure of 18th-century mathematics, connecting the calculus of Newton and Leibniz to later developments. His notation system (such as f(x), e, i, π, etc.) became the standard language of modern mathematics. In popular culture, Euler is often portrayed as a hardworking genius, particularly his perseverance in continuing research after becoming blind is widely celebrated. The mathematical community honors him with numerous concepts named 'Euler numbers,' 'Euler theorems,' 'Euler equations,' etc., indicating his ubiquitous influence. Euler's work reflects the unity of mathematics, connecting different fields, and this interdisciplinary thinking continues to offer important insights for modern science.

self.zh: 数学家们如果不想被外行人看作是空想家，就必须避免这种肤浅的看法。
self.en: Mathematicians should avoid this superficial view if they do not want to be regarded as dreamers by outsiders.

others.zh: 欧拉的计算就像呼吸一样自然，没有任何努力。
others.en: Euler's calculations are as natural as breathing, without any effort.
